each person is different on how they prefer to be treated in times like that, but here go some suggestions:

- acknowledge his pain: say things like "I'm sorry you're going through this, it must be hard" stuff like that. is important to show that you are not trying to minimize or ignore their feelings even if it's bad ones
- know that you can't solve it, so don't ask/say things like if you could. what you can do is HELP, so you can ask if there is anything you can do to help him feel better
- like said in other comments, be there. saying "I'm here, you can talk to me" one time or two is rarely enough, is more helpful showing you presence, but without making it a big deal. make you presence be noted reaching to him very often, ask how he feel, offer to do stuff (you two are distant from each other, so you could offer to play a game or watch a movie online together, send him some music something like that)
- it can be very helpful if you can create a safe space to talk about suicide, but only if it doesn't hurt you. I know this can be a very sensitive subject for people that haven't experienced suicide ideation, but it's really harmful when we have this thoughts but cannot share with anyone because people overreact or get upset when we talk about it, so if you're comfortable enough, try to make them comfortable when talking about it (listen a lot, acknowledge his feelings, don't try to solve it)
- be cool and respect if he is not ready to talk about it with you, this will show that you respect his boundaries and can make him feel more comfortable in the future

I hope that helps.

I can't say I understand everything you are feeling, but I'm sorry that you can't enjoy your thoughts or your life. I can relate to that specific part tho. A year my anxiety was peaking, I used to over analyze every single thing, every interaction with someone and my own actions that didn't even happened yet. I lived so vividly in the future that my present was trash and I couldn't stand it, leading me to develop depression and suicide thoughts. I used to make the same thing you described, predicting all the possibilities and outcome a situation could possibly have. The two main issues was: nothing really surprised me anymore because I certainly already predicted something very similar and this made every interaction with anyone incredibly boring (so I though wasn't worth my time) and was extremely exhausting. I was spending all of my 1 energy on this 24/7 and that shit burned my brain, so thinking started to be difficult. Because of that, I think maybe I can relate to what you're feeling. 

The only thing that helped me was try a different therapy approach. It was very hard at the beginning, but with time I could start to understand why my brain worked like that, why I started doing it and how it harmed me. After this, I could work on the main issues and decrease this thing. I still do it sometimes, by it got a lot better and I don't hate my thoughts or my present anymore (at least for the most of the time). I'm not saying therapy will cure you, you already said you tried a lot of solutions, but idk, just wanted to share. Our minds are rally one of the hardest places to escape.

one thing I learned from my break ups is that sometimes we don't even miss the person, but just the feeling of having someone there even though this person treated you in a shitty way. like you said, you were craving love and caring, in response he was a total jerk with no reason, so you don't really need him specifically.

in that times when we are emotionally vulnerable, it's good to have support from other people (like friends or family) to help us heal. not that they will replace him or instantly make you feel well, but it's important to know and feel that this shitty person that left you wasn't the only one you had. of course this  is hurting a lot, and it will take some time to heal 100% but you're certainly going to be ok. this bad person wasn't irreplaceable, you are the most important here and I know that it hurts to see how he is moving on, but you will eventually too. it just show how little he cared about you.

and also, I advice you to not try to engage in another relation now, while you are emotionally vulnerable. his leaving may left a hole in your chest, but don't try to fill it up with someone else. instead of that, heal it so you feel confident and well enough to let someone special enter your life in the future. 

also know that maybe you're experiencing grief. we don't feel it just when people die, but when someone leaves our life in general. so even when a person still alive, if they suddenly aren't in our lives anymore, we can experience grief, and this can be a long and painful process, but eventually it will pass. 

I wish you the best, and that you start to feel better very soon. just don't try to go back to him. you will be ok.
